events.text: {npc} has cooked your favourite dish, the one you never stopped asking for, and set out two bowls without saying anything.

effects.log: It tastes exactly as it always did. {npc} watches you eat and smiles the whole time.
You eat in five minutes. {npc} says nothing, and washes the bowls alone.

variants: {npc} has made the dish you always begged for as a child, and laid out two bowls, and says nothing about it at all.

events.text: {npc} sits with you by the stove and tells you a story about your grandfather, who once fought off a tiger with a rice pot.

effects.log: 'Mostly,' {npc} says. 'The pot was very large.'
You fall asleep in the middle of the third one. {npc} covers you with a blanket.

events.text: You find {npc} watching you train from the doorway. {He} has brought you a towel and a cup of barley tea, and pretends not to be proud.

effects.log: {npc} claps at every move like it is a festival. You have never performed for a better audience.

choices.text: Take the tea and keep going

effects.log: {npc} stays in the doorway until the sun goes down.

variants: {npc} is leaning in the doorway while you train, holding a towel and a cup of barley tea, and trying very hard not to look proud.

events.text: {npc}'s back is bad this year, and the harvest is going to rot in the field. {He} does not ask. {He} just looks at the field and sighs.

mem.note: brought in the harvest when my back was bad

effects.log: A week of dawn-to-dusk work. The granary is full. {npc} tells the whole village about it, twice.
The field is cleared. {npc} is grateful, and a little sad you did not come yourself.
Half the harvest rots. {npc} never mentions it. That is worse.

variants: {npc}'s back has given out this year, and the grain is going to rot standing. {He} does not ask for help. {He} just stands at the edge of the field and sighs.

events.text: A letter from home: {npc} has been coughing all winter and will not see a physician because it costs too much.

choices.text: Go home and bring a physician

effects.log: It was nearly pneumonia. The physician says another month would have been too late. {npc} scolds you for spending the money, holding your hand the whole time.
{npc} recovers by spring. The letter of thanks is mostly about how you should eat more.

choices.text: Write back that it is probably nothing

effects.log: It was not nothing. {npc} recovers, slowly, and something between you does not.

variants: A letter from home: {npc} has been coughing since the first frost and refuses to see a physician because of the cost.

events.text: {npc} presses a small cloth bundle into your hands: coins, saved one by one for years. 'For when you need it. Do not argue with me.'

effects.log: Sixty taels in copper and silver. You know exactly how long this took. You do not spend it for a long time.
You slip it back into {his} sewing basket that night. The next morning it is in your pack again. This goes on for a week.

variants: {npc} pushes a knotted handkerchief across the table. Inside are coins, years of them, saved a few at a time. 'For when you need it. And do not argue with me.'
Before you leave, {npc} slips a heavy little bundle into your sleeve: coins, put by one at a time for years. 'For a bad day. Not one word.'

events.text: {npc} has sewn you a new winter robe, lined with cotton, with a tiny crane stitched on the inside where only you will see it.

effects.log: You wear it every winter until it falls apart. You keep the crane.

variants: A parcel from {npc}: a winter robe, quilted thick, and on the inside of the collar a small crane in white thread, where nobody else will ever look.
{npc} has been sewing by lamplight for a month. The result is a padded winter robe with a little crane hidden inside the lining, just for you.

events.text: You learn that {npc} has been telling every matchmaker in the county how good-looking, kind and rich you are. Two of those are lies.

effects.log: Three matchmakers visit that month. You hide in the woodshed for all three.
{npc} agrees to stop. {He} does not stop.

events.text: {npc} is old now and moves slowly. {He} asks you to walk with {him} to the hill where the family graves are.

mem.note: walked with me to the graves

effects.log: {He} tells you the name of every ancestor under the pines. You realise, halfway down, that {he} is telling you so that someone remembers.
{npc} protests the whole way up and laughs the whole way down.

events.text: Caught in a downpour, you end up sheltering under the same roof as {npc}. There is nothing to do but talk.

mem.note: told me their dreams in the rain

effects.log: By the time the rain stops, you have both said more than you meant to.
{npc} eats half of it and then tells you a joke so bad you both laugh until the rain stops.

events.text: {npc} noticed a flaw in your stance and, awkwardly, offers to show you how to fix it.

effects.log: The fix is small. The difference is not. You buy {him} dinner.

choices.text: Say you know what you are doing

effects.log: Two months later you realise {he} was right. You never say so.

events.text: {npc} drags you to the Lantern Festival. 'You train too much. Tonight, you are a person.'

mem.note: came to the Lantern Festival with me

effects.log: Lanterns on the river, sweet rice balls, fireworks over the rooftops. For one night, the murim does not exist.
You leave before the fireworks. You hear them from the training yard.

events.text: {npc} asks for your help: {his} younger brother has joined a gang and will not come home.

ok.log: You talk to the boy for an hour. He comes home. {npc} does not know how to thank you, so {he} just hugs you.

mem.note: tried to bring my brother home

fail.log: The gang does not want to talk. You fight your way out. The boy watches, and thinks about it.

effects.log: {npc} nods and walks away. {He} does not ask you for anything again.

events.text: {npc} cannot read, and has received a letter {he} is afraid of. {He} asks you to read it aloud.

effects.log: It is from {his} long-lost sister. {npc} cries. You read it three more times.
It takes a month. The first thing {npc} ever reads alone is that letter.

events.text: {npc} catches up with you at dusk, out of breath. 'Do not take the east road tomorrow. I cannot say how I know. You {debt}; now we are even.'

effects.log: You take the west road. Two days later, you hear what happened on the east one.
There were men waiting. You get through. {npc} was right, and {he} will remind you forever.

events.text: {npc} has not forgotten that you {debt_of}. {He} has nothing to give but one thing: a technique from {his} family, never taught to outsiders.

effects.log: It is only a breathing rhythm. It is the most useful thing anyone has ever given you.

choices.text: Refuse: a family secret should stay in the family

effects.log: {npc} bows deeply. Your refusal meant more to {him} than the technique ever could.

events.text: You hear a story in a teahouse about a hero who fought off twenty bandits. It is about you. It was four bandits. {npc} has been telling it.

effects.log: Nobody believes the correction. By next month, it is thirty bandits.
By spring, you also killed a dragon. You buy {npc} a drink, and also warn {him} to stop.

events.text: Word reaches you that {npc} has been telling people you {grudge_of}, and a great deal more that is not true at all.

ok.log: You calmly take the lies apart one by one in front of everyone. {npc} leaves red-faced.

fail.log: It turns into a shouting match. People believe whoever shouts last. That is {npc}.

effects.log: It stings for a season. Then people stop listening to {npc}.

events.text: {npc} tosses a wooden sword at your feet. 'I have been training. Let us see who is better now.'

ok.log: You win, narrowly. {npc} groans, then demands a rematch next year.

mem.note: let me win, or did they?

fail.log: {npc} wins and is unbearable about it for a week.

effects.log: 'Coward,' {npc} says, grinning. You share a meal instead.

events.text: Letters have been appearing under your door, unsigned, in careful handwriting you slowly realise belongs to {npc}.

effects.log: Letters become walks. Walks become a habit. One evening, {npc} holds your hand and neither of you mentions it.

choices.text: Tell {him} kindly that you are not ready

effects.log: {npc} smiles bravely. The letters stop. You keep the ones you received.

events.text: {npc} invites you to share a pot of good tea, just the two of you, like old times. Your cup smells faintly of almonds, and {npc} does not drink first.

choices.text: Take the cup. It is {npc}. You trust {him}.

ok.log: You only touch it to your lips. The world tilts. You wake three days later in a ditch, alive by some miracle, and understand everything.

fail.log: You only touch it to your lips. The last thing you see is {npc} looking away.

choices.text: Swap the cups while {he} looks away

ok.log: {npc} drinks the cup meant for you, and realises what has happened a moment too late.

fail.log: {npc} sees you swap them. In the struggle, some of it goes down your throat.

choices.text: Set the cup down and watch {his} face

effects.log: You set the cup down, slowly. {npc}'s smile does not move, but {his} eyes do. You both know. {He} leaves before dawn.

choices.text: (You remember this) Knock the cup from {his} hand

effects.log: The tea hisses on the floor where it lands. In another life it reached your lips. Not this time. {npc} stares at you as if you had read {his} mind. In a way, you did.
